par-iter.title: How rayon's par_iter works
par-iter.description: A parallel iterator over references: the work is split across threads.

note.text: like iter(), but on all CPU cores

slides.caption: rayon splits the collection into pieces, runs them on a pool of threads, and combines the results.
Each thread squares its own part of the items.
The partial sums are added together.
Change iter() to par_iter(): the rest of the chain usually stays the same.

par-iter-mut.title: How rayon's par_iter_mut works
par-iter-mut.description: A parallel iterator over mutable references.

slides.caption: Each element is touched by exactly one thread.

into-par-iter.title: How rayon's into_par_iter works (Vec)
into-par-iter.description: A parallel iterator that takes ownership of the Vec's items.

par-bridge.title: How rayon's par_bridge works
par-bridge.description: Turns any Send iterator into a parallel iterator.

slides.caption: Items are handed out one by one; the order is not kept.
Prefer par_iter on collections: it splits better.

map.title: How ParallelIterator::map works
map.description: Applies a function to every item, in parallel.

slides.caption: The closure must be Fn + Sync + Send: no shared mutable state.
map_init gives each thread its own scratch value.

filter.title: How ParallelIterator::filter works
filter.description: Keeps the items that pass a test, in parallel.

slides.caption: filter_map tests and maps at once.

filter-map.title: How ParallelIterator::filter_map works
filter-map.description: Maps to an Option and keeps the Somes.

flat-map.title: How ParallelIterator::flat_map works
flat-map.description: Maps each item to many and flattens them.

for-each.title: How ParallelIterator::for_each works
for-each.description: Runs a closure for every item, in parallel and in no particular order.

slides.caption: Shared results need atomics or a Mutex.
Do not rely on any order.

sum.title: How ParallelIterator::sum works
sum.description: Adds all items using several threads.

slides.caption: Partial sums are combined; for floats the rounding may differ from a sequential sum.

reduce.title: How ParallelIterator::reduce works
reduce.description: Combines items with an associative function and an identity value.

slides.caption: Each thread starts from identity() and combines its items; then the partial results are combined the same way.
The function must be associative, or results vary between runs.

reduce-with.title: How ParallelIterator::reduce_with works
reduce-with.description: Like reduce without an identity; None for an empty input.

fold.title: How ParallelIterator::fold works
fold.description: Folds each piece separately, giving one partial result per piece.

slides.caption: fold yields several partial results; finish with sum or reduce.
Each piece folds to a partial sum.
Handy when the accumulator is a Vec or HashMap.
len() is instant for indexed iterators.

min.title: How ParallelIterator::min works
min.description: The smallest item; None if empty.

slides.caption: Ties: any of the equal minimums may be returned.

max-by-key.title: How ParallelIterator::max_by_key works
max-by-key.description: The item with the largest key.

slides.caption: Ties may return any of them.

any.title: How ParallelIterator::any works
any.description: true if any item passes; other threads stop early once one is found.

slides.caption: Stops early at the first failure.

find-any.title: How ParallelIterator::find_any works
find-any.description: Some item that matches: not necessarily the first one.

slides.caption: Whichever thread finds a match first wins.

find-first.title: How ParallelIterator::find_first works
find-first.description: The first matching item in the original order.

slides.caption: Slower than find_any: later matches must wait.

collect.title: How ParallelIterator::collect works
collect.description: Gathers the results into a collection, keeping the order for indexed iterators.

partition.title: How ParallelIterator::partition works
partition.description: Splits items into two collections by a test.

slides.caption: Both collections keep the original order.
partition_map can change the items too.

copied.title: How ParallelIterator::copied works
copied.description: Turns &T items into T for Copy types.

slides.caption: cloned() does the same for Clone types.

try-for-each.title: How ParallelIterator::try_for_each works
try-for-each.description: Runs a fallible closure on every item; stops early on the first error found.

slides.caption: Which error is returned is not fixed when several fail.

map-init.title: How ParallelIterator::map_init works
map-init.description: Like map, with a value created once per piece of work (e.g. a buffer or RNG).

slides.caption: init runs once per split, not once per item.
map_with clones a given value instead.

enumerate.title: How IndexedParallelIterator::enumerate works
enumerate.description: Pairs each item with its index.

slides.caption: Only for indexed iterators (from Vec, slices, ranges...).

zip.title: How IndexedParallelIterator::zip works
zip.description: Pairs items of two indexed parallel iterators.

slides.caption: Stops at the shorter one; zip_eq panics on different lengths.

chunks.title: How IndexedParallelIterator::chunks works
chunks.description: Groups items into Vecs of n.

slides.caption: The last chunk may be shorter.
par_chunks works on slices without moving.

position-first.title: How IndexedParallelIterator::position_first works
position-first.description: The index of the first matching item.

slides.caption: position_any returns any matching index, faster.

with-min-len.title: How IndexedParallelIterator::with_min_len works
with-min-len.description: Stops rayon from splitting work into pieces smaller than n items.

slides.caption: Splitting has a cost; for very cheap items bigger pieces are faster.

collect-into-vec.title: How IndexedParallelIterator::collect_into_vec works
collect-into-vec.description: Collects into an existing Vec, reusing its memory.

rev.title: How IndexedParallelIterator::rev works
rev.description: Reverses the order of an indexed parallel iterator.

par-sort.title: How ParallelSliceMut::par_sort works
par-sort.description: Sorts a slice using several threads (stable merge sort).

slides.caption: The slice is split, the parts are sorted on different threads, then merged.
Sort the halves in parallel: [3, 5] and [1, 8].
Worth it for large slices; small ones sort faster with sort().

par-sort-unstable.title: How ParallelSliceMut::par_sort_unstable works
par-sort-unstable.description: Parallel unstable sort (quicksort-style), usually the fastest.

slides.caption: par_sort keeps equal items in order.

par-sort-by-key.title: How ParallelSliceMut::par_sort_by_key works
par-sort-by-key.description: Parallel stable sort by a key.

par-chunks.title: How ParallelSlice::par_chunks works
par-chunks.description: Processes a slice in chunks of n, in parallel.

slides.caption: The last chunk may be shorter.

par-chunks-mut.title: How ParallelSliceMut::par_chunks_mut works
par-chunks-mut.description: Mutable chunks of a slice, processed in parallel.

slides.caption: Each chunk is owned by one thread.
Common in image processing (rows of pixels).

par-windows.title: How ParallelSlice::par_windows works
par-windows.description: Overlapping windows of n items, in parallel.

par-lines.title: How ParallelString::par_lines works
par-lines.description: The lines of a string, as a parallel iterator.

slides.caption: Line breaks are removed, like str::lines.

par-split-whitespace.title: How ParallelString::par_split_whitespace works
par-split-whitespace.description: The words of a string, in parallel.

par-extend.title: How ParallelExtend::par_extend works (Vec)
par-extend.description: Extends a Vec with the results of a parallel iterator.

slides.caption: Order is kept for indexed iterators.

max.title: How ParallelIterator::max works
max.description: The largest item, found in parallel; None if empty.

slides.caption: Ties may return any of the equal items.
